headline: 3 pistols and 77 rounds recovered as top criminal ‘Auto Sajal’ arrested in Dhaka
summary: Police seized weapons suspected to be looted from police stations, along with narcotics, following a raid in the Shamibagh area.
details: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) have arrested four people, including the notorious criminal 'Auto Sajal', following raids in the Wari and Gendaria areas.
During the operation, police recovered three modern pistols and 77 rounds of ammunition, as well as a significant amount of narcotics.
Additional Police Commissioner S N Nazrul Islam announced the details during a press conference at the DMP Media Center on Saturday.
The arrests follow an investigation into an incident on March 2, where a gang fired at police during a raid in Wari and managed to escape.
Police suspect that the recovered firearms were looted from police stations.
Two separate cases have been filed against the arrested individuals at the Gendaria police station.
caption:
A notorious crime boss and three others arrested in Dhaka with looted police weapons and drugs.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) have arrested four people, including the notorious criminal 'Auto Sajal', following raids in the Wari and Gendaria areas.

During the operation, police recovered three modern pistols and 77 rounds of ammunition, as well as a significant amount of narcotics.

Additional Police Commissioner S N Nazrul Islam announced the details during a press conference at the DMP Media Center on Saturday.

The arrests follow an investigation into an incident on March 2, where a gang fired at police during a raid in Wari and managed to escape.

Police suspect that the recovered firearms were looted from police stations.

Two separate cases have been filed against the arrested individuals at the Gendaria police station.

headline_marked: Australia posts [[record 196-5 total against Bangladesh]] in 2nd T20I
headline: Australia posts record 196-5 total against Bangladesh in 2nd T20I
summary: Matt Renshaw's career-best 89* and Tim David's 45 powered Australia to their highest-ever T20I score against the Tigers in Chattogram.
details: Australia posted a formidable 196 for five in their 20 overs during the second T20I against Bangladesh at the Bir Shrestha Shaheed Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman Stadium in Chattogram on Friday.
Matt Renshaw led the charge with a career-best unbeaten 89 off 52 balls, smashing four fours and five sixes. Tim David provided strong support with a brisk 45 off 26 balls.
This total marks Australia's highest-ever T20I score against Bangladesh, surpassing their previous best of 158 for three achieved in Mirpur in 2014.

Bangladesh had a promising start, reducing Australia to 44 for three within the powerplay. However, a 97-run partnership between Renshaw and David for the fourth wicket shifted the momentum decisively.
For the Tigers, Nasum Ahmed was the standout bowler, claiming 2-27 from his four overs. The rest of the bowling attack struggled, with all other bowlers conceding more than 8.5 runs per over.
Australia captain Mitchell Marsh won the toss and elected to bat first. Bangladesh entered the match trailing 1-0 in the three-match series after a four-wicket defeat in the opening game.
caption:
A record-breaking day for Australia! 🇦🇺

Matt Renshaw's career-best 89* helps Australia post their highest-ever T20I total against Bangladesh.

Australia posted a formidable 196 for five in their 20 overs during the second T20I against Bangladesh at the Bir Shrestha Shaheed Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman Stadium in Chattogram on Friday.

Matt Renshaw led the charge with a career-best unbeaten 89 off 52 balls, smashing four fours and five sixes. Tim David provided strong support with a brisk 45 off 26 balls.

This total marks Australia's highest-ever T20I score against Bangladesh, surpassing their previous best of 158 for three achieved in Mirpur in 2014.

Bangladesh had a promising start, reducing Australia to 44 for three within the powerplay. However, a 97-run partnership between Renshaw and David for the fourth wicket shifted the momentum decisively.

For the Tigers, Nasum Ahmed was the standout bowler, claiming 2-27 from his four overs. The rest of the bowling attack struggled, with all other bowlers conceding more than 8.5 runs per over.

Australia captain Mitchell Marsh won the toss and elected to bat first. Bangladesh entered the match trailing 1-0 in the three-match series after a four-wicket defeat in the opening game.
